purpose: Dichlorphenamide is used to treat periodic paralysis, which is a condition where you experience sudden episodes of muscle weakness or temporary paralysis. It helps reduce how often these episodes happen and how severe they are. It is approved for both hypokalemic and hyperkalemic forms of periodic paralysis.
how_it_works: This medication works by blocking an enzyme in your body called carbonic anhydrase. By blocking this enzyme, it helps keep the levels of potassium in your blood more stable. Stable potassium levels help prevent the muscle weakness episodes that happen with periodic paralysis.
common_side_effects: You may feel confused or have trouble thinking clearly. Some people feel tingling or numbness in their hands, feet, or face. You might also feel tired, dizzy, or have an upset stomach. Decreased appetite and weight loss can also occur.
warnings: This medication can lower the level of potassium in your blood, so your doctor will monitor your potassium regularly. It can also cause a dangerous build-up of acid in your blood called metabolic acidosis, so tell your doctor right away if you feel very tired, have trouble breathing, or feel confused. Avoid taking it with alcohol or other medications that can also affect acid-base balance. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems before starting this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 50 mg taken by mouth two times a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond and how well you tolerate the medication. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not change your dose on your own.
